No, this is not correct. In Switzerland, you can switch your basic health insurance provider at any time, and there is **no specific deadline** like December 31st required for the switch to be valid in the new year. You can change insurers throughout the year.

However, you must ensure that you do not have any outstanding premiums or debts with your current insurer at the time of the switch, as that could complicate the process. Also, the new insurer must accept you (eligibility criteria can apply). It's also a good idea to switch before the end of the year if you want the new insurer to apply changes like adjusted premiums or deductibles from January 1st, but it is not a legal requirement.

For accurate and official information, always refer to the official guidelines from the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) or your current insurance provider.
